findings.quote: YAML lets you write a short set of keys between braces, and a single branch can stand in for a list. So `push: {branches: main}` means the same as Brad’s three lines under `push:`.
findings.problem: I checked the flagged claim and it is true, but the lesson gives YAML the credit. Braces are YAML (a flow mapping). Accepting one string where a list is expected is a rule of GitHub's workflow parser: the schema defines `branches` as one-of a string or a sequence. In YAML itself, `main` and `[main]` are different values. Also, Brad's block has two lines under `push:` (`branches:` and `- main`). The one-liner replaces three lines only if you count `push:` itself.
findings.fix: YAML lets you write a short set of keys on one line between braces, and GitHub accepts a single branch name where it expects a list. So `push: {branches: main}` means the same as Brad’s three lines from `push:` down to `- main`.

result.summary:
The lesson is factually solid. I found no wrong commands, no private or stale leftovers, and every quiz has exactly one defensible answer, apart from the timing ambiguity in check-13. The lesson validator prints ok.

All four flagged claims check out:
1. `gh run list -R actions/checkout --workflow licensed.yml --status success --limit 5` uses real flags (`success` is a valid `--status` value). The lesson's column description matches gh's table: STATUS, TITLE, WORKFLOW, BRANCH, EVENT, ID, ELAPSED, AGE. Recent successful Licensed runs exist (Oct 2026), so their logs are still inside the retention window.
2. gh prefixes every `--log` line with `<job name>\t<step name>\t`, so each line does start with `Check licenses`. Real 2026 job logs end the Set up job part with `Complete job name: <job name>`, after the GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions group and before `##[group]Run actions/checkout…` with `token: ***`. All four things the Try it asks for fall well within `head -80`.
3. A single branch string really is accepted: the workflow schema defines `event-branches` as one-of a string or a sequence. The claim holds, but it's GitHub's parser rule, not YAML's (see finding).
4. runner-images #14748 says the ubuntu-latest move to 26.04 rolls out "beginning October 19, 2026", finishing by Nov 19.

Other checks that passed:
- The lesson's `licensed.yml` and `test.yml` copies match the live files in actions/checkout, and its Brad ci.yml matches both the gist and cicd-lab's ci.yml.
- The gist does tell you to run `npm ci` and `npm run verify` before pushing.
- These GitHub Docs claims are current: the permissions none-rule, the 360-minute default, timed-out jobs ending as cancelled, `schedule` `timezone` support, `pull_request_target` running from the default branch, `workflow_dispatch` checks not counting, and the merge-conflict no-run rule.
- Vercel's `repository_dispatch` event names, Deployment Checks' job-name matching, and the setup-node cache facts are current too.
- The video title and date in sources are correct.

Findings: one medium (the "Expected, no run" flashcard contradicts check-16 and the cheat sheet) and nine low:
- the lab is said to have an agent add ci.yml, but Step 4 does it by hand;
- the gh setup link should go to What Git and GitHub are;
- check-13's "a minute apart" timing is ambiguous;
- the licensed.yml bullet credits YAML for GitHub's single-branch rule and miscounts Brad's lines;
- check-node's "`engines` never switches" is too absolute;
- Brad, `uses:`/`run:`, `engines`, the lockfile and `[main]` list syntax are each used before they're explained.

The gates lesson holds up well. I checked every claim against current sources: GitHub's rulesets, required checks and troubleshooting docs; Vercel's Deployment Checks, Instant Rollback, Deployment Protection, Environments and build docs; the live Render-to-Vercel migration guide (fetched with no cache); Render's deploy, health-check and preview docs; Brad's gist; and his transcript and chapter times. All of them match. That covers both rules a new ruleset starts with selected, the seven-day rule, required checks passing on the latest commit, skipped jobs counting as success with the always()/needs advice, "Waiting for status to be reported", the Settings → Build and Deployment → Deployment Checks path, Force Promote, the Typecheck script names, the Hobby/Pro rollback reach, and "Auto-assign Custom Production Domains". The Brad narration (24:16 test, disable, merge, Render starts no deploy, revert, re-enable) matches the video. Every /learn link points at a lesson that provides what is promised: the lab sets up a single `Verify` Deployment Check and runs the failing-test experiment, your-projects-pipeline's prompt adds the Verify job first, and the other links cover revert, merge vs squash commits and classic protection. Every question has exactly one right answer, with sound Why lines. I found no leftovers (no Care4Mind, private repos, lesson numbers or dated checks), and the validator prints ok. Flagged claim settled: `gh ruleset check --default`, `gh run list --limit 5`, `gh pr list --state all --limit 3` and `gh pr view <n> --web` are real. Per the cli/cli source, ruleset check prints "N rules apply to branch main in repo OWNER/REPO" followed by one "- <type>" line per rule, and run list has an EVENT column. Several independent reports confirm that GET rules/branches returns HTTP 403 ("Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public…") on private Free repos. Remaining problems are minor: the Try it doesn't help a reader interpret empty or partial output (no runs, non-required checks, which rule is the merge gate), plus a few precision fixes.

findings.quote: No `push` runs means a merged commit never gets a check of its own, so a release gate would wait forever.
findings.problem: `gh run list --limit 5` shows only the 5 newest runs of any event. An agent that pushes several commits to a PR branch fills those 5 with `pull_request` runs, so finding no `push` run there doesn't prove the workflow lacks a push trigger. Also, the reader's practice `recipes` repo (made in What Git and GitHub are / Push, pull and remotes) has no workflow, so the command prints `no runs found`. The step never says what that means; it only says "You should see your CI workflow's runs".
findings.fix: Add a filtered command and explain both outcomes: "gh run list --branch main --event push --limit 5". Then: "If the first command prints `no runs found`, the repo has no workflow yet, so no gate has a check to wait for. If this one finds none although you've merged since the workflow was added, the workflow doesn't run on `push`: look for `push` under its `on:`."

result.summary:
The lab mostly holds up. I found 8 real problems: 4 medium, 4 low.

Checked and correct:
- All video timestamps match transcript.md.
- The gist's commands, code, commit messages, PR title and public-repo advice match Brad's gist.
- Vercel's Express entrypoint list matches its docs and packages/express/src/build.ts.
- Deployment Checks match Vercel's docs: Add Checks, the GitHub provider, the two prerequisites, Force Promote, and checks matched by job name.
- Standard Protection is on by default for new projects, and the Production URL stays public.
- On the GitHub side:
  - Rulesets work on public repos only on GitHub Free.
  - A new ruleset starts as Disabled.
  - The rules call leaves out disabled rulesets.
  - The Revert flow matches GitHub's docs.
- Node 24 via `engines` matches Vercel's docs.
- TypeScript 6.0.3 exists, and the TS6 fix keeps `npm run verify` passing in a local run.
- Every /learn link points at a lesson that covers the topic: gates (look gate), what-ci-cd-is, push-pull-and-remotes, undo-and-conflicts, your-projects-pipeline. The lab doesn't rely on the practice project, its `test` workflow or auto-merge.
- No leftovers, and the validator prints ok.

Flagged claims, settled:
- TS2688 and "move to TypeScript 6": keep. This is consistent with Vercel's current source: @vercel/node's TypeScript 7 path compiles through a temporary tsconfig in the system temp folder. The experimental-builder crash (vercel/vercel#17390) is real and still open. The TS6 fix keeps `npm run verify` passing locally.
- "Auto-assign Custom Production Domains": correct. It's under Settings → Environments → Production → Branch Tracking.
- Vercel button names: Import Git Repository / Import, Adjust GitHub App Permissions and Visit Preview are correct. "Add New…" is out of date; the button is now "Create New" (lgp-3).

- Squash merging instead of Brad's merge commits: the lesson states it.
- The e2e YAML, `disableRepositoryDispatchEvents` and Ignored Build Step items aren't in this lesson.

Main problems:
- The explanation of `git branch -d` after a squash is wrong for the lab's own flow. Without `git fetch --prune`, `-d` deletes the branch with a warning instead of refusing. I reproduced this.
- A missing lock file fails CI at Set up Node.js (setup-node's `cache: npm`), not at `npm ci`.
- The Vercel button is now "Create New", not "Add New…".
- Step 3's Try it expects a Ready deployment, but the lesson itself says the TypeScript 7 starter fails, and the box doesn't point to the fix.

Smaller problems: the cause given for the "No entrypoint found" error, "through both gates" contradicting the step order, a production-only variable scenario that clashes with the lesson's own TypeScript 7 note, and the verify output description.

I checked the whole lesson against the live sources. The review notes have no flagged claims for it.

The sources were: Claude Code's GitHub Actions and Authentication docs; claude-code-action's repo (security.md, usage.md, faq.md, capabilities doc, token.ts, mode detector); Matt's spec and workflow files at course-video-manager main (4 Nov 2026); Sandcastle's docs at main (5 Nov 2026); the to-tickets Skill (main is identical to the snapshot); the AI Hero dictionary pages for AFK, HITL and software factory; GitHub's docs on GITHUB_TOKEN, pull_request_target, secure use, labels, billing and script injection; GitHub's changelog; Vercel's Deployment Checks docs; and the linked lessons.

The validator prints ok (9 final tests, 23 checkpoints). There are no private-project leftovers, old-site features or "Lesson N" references.

Most of the lesson holds up:
- The review YAML matches the docs exactly (claude-plugins-official, checkout@v6).
- Interactive and automation modes are right, and the action's code confirms the prompt-changes-mode answer.
- The setup steps, app permissions, setup-token (one year, paid plan) and the write-access and bot checks are right.
- Every row of the platform table matches the spec, as do the labels, AGENT_PAT and the graceful fallback, the concurrency groups with cancel-in-progress false, Promote Queued's issues: write, the pull_request_target reason and noSandbox().

What needs fixing:
- **Two medium fact errors.** First, @claude on an open pull request pushes to that pull request's own branch, not a new one. Second, Actions minutes are free on public repos with standard runners, and the lab tells readers to make cicd-lab public.
